findings.summary: The browser-only async readback (AdvanceAsyncReadback) and the emdawnwebgpu JS path are GPU code CI cannot run: node has no WebGPU and Initialize fails before a device exists, so this code is compiled but never executed by any test
findings.scenario: At G5, when a device is handed in, a mistake in the map/unmap/padding logic (e.g. reading a buffer whose map was aborted by a resize or Shutdown) would surface only in a real browser; acknowledged in dev.json 'unverified', to be covered at G5

findings.summary: Comment says CreateWebGpuRenderer is 'Declared only where the backend is compiled in', but the header declares it unconditionally (no N2ENGINE_RENDERER_WEBGPU guard); it is only DEFINED where the backend is compiled
findings.scenario: A native translation unit that includes the header in a build with the backend OFF compiles and then fails at link time instead of at compile time, contrary to what the comment promises

findings.summary: The isHeadless option row and the 'Headless mode' intro still name only SOFTWARE (and WEBGPU) as the no-window exceptions; RenderBackend::NONE also creates no window, and does so whatever isHeadless says (InitWindow returns early before UsesNoWindow is checked)
findings.scenario: A reader of the options table alone may think NONE with isHeadless=false opens a GLFW window; the #no-renderer section linked from the renderBackend row states the real behaviour, so this is wording only
